papers.summary: We develop a general statistical framework for inverse obstacle imaging and resolution analysis from far-field second moments under random illumination. The regularized $Q$-statistic is introduced and utilized to measure the minimal statistically weighted cost of synthesizing the test far field associated with a sampling point. Its reciprocal provides an imaging indicator. Under uniform full-aperture plane-wave illumination, we relate this indicator to several classical sampling indicators and derive their statistical counterparts for general random illumination. For the resolution analysis, separating the effects of radiation and noise from the statistics of induced boundary sources, we measure a correlation-free resolution limit by the one-sided half-height width of the boundary transition. In the regime of fixed wavenumber $k$ with the noise-calibrated regularization level $ρ_τ\to 0$, we establish a sharp asymptotic law for this width for simply connected domains with analytic boundaries. The width scales as \(h_Γ(x)\log\log(1/ρ_τ)/\log(1/ρ_τ)\), with $h_Γ(x)$ a geometric prefactor along the boundary determining both the boundary image contrast and the local transition width. For general boundary-source statistics, we examine how the source mean, variance, and correlation affect imaging quality. Finally, in representative scattering configurations, we provide qualitative interpretations of some typical imaging phenomena through the statistical structure of their induced boundary sources. Numerical examples illustrate these mechanisms and indicate that practical resolution is governed jointly by source statistics, radiation, the noise level, rather than by wavelength alone.
papers.title: A Statistical Imaging Framework for Inverse Obstacle Scattering and Its Resolution Analysis

papers.summary: We establish the strong convergence of a fully discrete equidistant tamed Euler--Maruyama (ETEM) method for time-changed stochastic delay differential equations (TCSDDEs) with state-dependent $\mathrm{d}t$ drifts. A coupled one-sided condition on the subordinator-driven drift and diffusion allows superlinear coefficients with polynomial growth in both the current and delayed states. For subordinators whose Laplace exponent satisfies $ψ(λ)\geq c_1λ^α$ for all sufficiently large $λ$, with $α\in(0,1)$, we derive strong error bounds in terms of the time step $Δ$ and the subordinator sampling step $δ$, without imposing a relationship between them. Comparing the partitions generated by the exact and approximate inverse subordinators controls the sampling error without introducing a factor proportional to the number of time steps. For coefficients Lipschitz in both time arguments and Lipschitz history, the scheme achieves a strong convergence rate of order $Δ^{α/2}(1+|\logΔ|)^{(1-α)/2}+\sqrt{δ(1+|\logδ|)}$. A terminal lower bound $c(Δ^{α/2}+δ^{1/2})$ for a multiplicative-noise equation with a stable subordinator establishes the sharpness of both polynomial exponents for this Euler scheme. Numerical experiments illustrate convergence for nonautonomous and multidimensional superlinear delay equations, as well as delay equations with low-regularity time dependence.
papers.title: Strong Convergence of Fully Discrete Tamed Euler Approximations for Time-Changed Stochastic Delay Differential Equations

papers.summary: The classical Newton-Maclaurin's inequalities for the elementary symmetric means are well known. In this paper, we derive a new class of Newton-type inequalities and generalize Maclaurin's inequality by connecting the elementary symmetric functions with their counterparts. Our idea is mainly motivated by the inclusion relations of G$\mathring{\text{a}}$rding's cones and $k$-convex cones.
papers.title: New Newton-type inequality and a unified perspective on Maclaurin's inequality via the inclusion relations of cones

papers.summary: We present a direct boundary integral equation (BIE) formulation of the Bloch eigenvalue problem for two-dimensional photonic crystals that uses only the free-space Helmholtz Green function. The unknowns are the Cauchy data of the Bloch mode on the inclusion boundary and on two cell walls. On the inclusion boundary, the transmission conditions are imposed via Müller's formulation. The wall equations, in turn, come from a stack formulation, in which Green's formula is applied on stacks of three cells, so that the wall self-interactions and the interactions between arcs sharing endpoints cancel exactly. The resulting system is of the second kind, Fredholm of index zero, and free of corner singularities, and the walls may be curved to keep the cell boundary away from the inclusions. Its operators are assembled once per frequency and reused for all Bloch vectors. We prove that every Bloch mode yields a nonzero null vector, and that a null vector comes from a Bloch mode exactly when its cell representation vanishes outside the cell, which gives an inexpensive test for spurious null vectors. The band frequencies are computed with a high-order Nyström discretization and the search of Bruno, Santana and Trefethen, which locates them as poles of adaptive Antoulas--Anderson (AAA) rational approximants to a randomly scalarized resolvent sampled on the real frequency axis. Numerical examples validate the method against exact and published band structures and include a challenging triangular lattice of air pores in a dielectric, whose cell requires curved walls.
papers.title: Photonic band structure by direct second-kind free-space boundary integral equations

papers.summary: We establish o-minimal definability results and develop point-counting machinery applicable to the zeros of a Bessel function of fixed non-negative real parameter. We also give an Ax-Schanuel theorem for Bessel functions of fixed (complex) parameters and exponential functions. We combine these to prove a sparsity result (weak Manin-Mumford) for points on an algebraic variety whose coordinates are zeros of a Bessel function of fixed (non-negative real) parameter. We apply this result to improve density results on spectral sets for the unit ball motivated by Fuglede's conjecture.
papers.title: Counting Bessel zeros and applications

papers.summary: This article presents an axiomatization of linear differential equations that is complete for topologically open properties with compact initial conditions and time horizons by proving them deductively via a sound reduction to formulas of linear real arithmetic. Indeed, linearity is preserved: linear differential invariants are complete for open properties of linear differential equations and reduce with a linear number of Lie derivatives (per atom) to linear real arithmetic. In particular, this article shows that the linear fragment of differential dynamic logic (dL), a modal extension of standard first-order logic over the reals satisfies these completeness properties. By establishing completeness within decidable linear real arithmetic, the need for proving sophisticated nonlinear formulas of real arithmetic is circumvented. Furthermore, this article establishes generalizations to the nonlinear fragment of dL that enable the practical certification of reachability computations, validating the output of external computations in dL with machine-checkable proofs.
papers.title: Linear Axiomatization of Linear Differential Equations

papers.summary: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces

papers.summary: Large-scale 3D peridynamic transient diffusion simulations are constrained by the computational cost and memory requirements of nonlocal interactions. We propose a fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT algorithm based on the recently developed asymptotically compatible finite difference (ACFD) scheme. By exploiting the discrete operator's structure and finite interaction range, the algorithm combines FFT acceleration with local inter-GPU communication. It preserves the ACFD scheme while avoiding the global data redistribution required by full 3D FFTs. We build a matrix-free GPU conjugate gradient (CG) solver, use multigrid preconditioning to reduce iteration counts, and introduce a human-audited configuration agent for efficient cross-level configuration. Strong-scaling tests show that sliced FFT-CG achieves 93.2% parallel efficiency on eight GPUs, compared with 28.2% for full FFT-CG on the same problem and hardware. The framework supports approximately 10.29 billion degrees of freedom on eight RTX 4090 GPUs with 24 GB of memory each. The insulated penny-shaped cutout benchmark demonstrates transient simulation with approximately 8.58 billion degrees of freedom. Three-dimensional star-shaped interface evolution further demonstrates convergence toward the local solution in a nonlinear phase-field problem. These results demonstrate that sliced FFT provides a scalable multi-GPU approach for fast computation of 3D peridynamic diffusion.
papers.title: Fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT solvers for asymptotically compatible discretizations of 3D nonlocal diffusion problems

papers.summary: We introduce and analyze a numerical framework for a class of first-order, non-local Mean Field Game (MFG) systems with two sources of low regularity: the time-dependent data are merely measurable, and the Hamiltonian is only of class $C^{1,1}$ with respect to the momentum variable. The proposed method combines a semi-Lagrangian approximation of the Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman equation with a Lagrange--Galerkin discretization of the continuity equation. Temporal measurability is handled by averaging the data over the time-grid intervals and using the stability theory of $L^1$-viscosity solutions. The limited regularity of the Hamiltonian is addressed through arguments from nonsmooth analysis, based in particular on Clarke's generalized differential calculus. We prove that the discrete solutions converge, up to some subsequence, to a solution of the MFG system. As a consequence, the numerical approximation also provides a constructive existence result. Under a monotonicity assumption on the coupling terms, we show that the solution to the MFG system is unique, implying the convergence of the whole sequence of discrete solutions. Finally, numerical experiments in one and two spatial dimensions illustrate the robustness of the method, including a linear--quadratic example with a running cost that is discontinuous in time and for which we compute an exact solution.
papers.title: First-Order Mean Field Games with Time-Measurable and $C ^{1,1}$ Hamiltonians: Analysis and Approximation

papers.summary: Consider the space of $C^\infty$-functions on the two-dimensional sphere $S^2$ and its decomposition $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ into a direct sum of minimal rotation-invariant spaces. We consider elements of $\oplus\mathcal H_m$ as functions of two variables, a nonnegative integer variable $m$ and a complex variable $u$ (a restriction of such function to a set $m=k$ is a polynomial in $u$ of degree $\le 2k$). The group $\mathrm{GL}\,(3,{\mathbb R})$ of all matrices of order 3 acts on $S^2$, so its Lie algebra acts in $C^\infty(S^2)$ by differentiations along vector fields. We construct operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$ corresponding such differentiations and obtain a collection of differential-difference operators in $\mathcal W^\infty$. The expressions include shifts $m\mapsto m\pm 2$ and derivatives of order 4 in $u$.
papers.title: Spherical harmonics and infinitesimal projective transformations

papers.summary: Motivated by the existence of closed maximal $\mathcal{I}$-eventually different ($\mathcal{I}$-MED) families, we study uniform combinatorial properties of ideals. For a fixed ideal, a property is uniform if its witnesses can be chosen by a single Borel map. We prove that every $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ ideal is uniformly weakly $P^+$. We also prove that the classes of Farah and weakly Farah ideals coincide, answering a question of Hrušák and Meza-Alcántara. We then show that every weakly Farah ideal is uniformly weakly Ramsey. As an application, we obtain closed $\mathcal{I}$-MED families for $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ ideals and weakly Farah ideals.
papers.title: Closed maximal eventually different families for $\boldsymbolΣ^0_3$ and weakly Farah ideals

papers.summary: In the context of intergenerational equity it is natural to ask that social welfare orders have th properties of finite anonymity and strong Pareto efficiency. Such social welfare orders can be constructed from nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers, and the existence of ultrafilters of this kind is known to be equivalent to the existence of a fair voting system for a countably infinite population in the sense of Arrow's theorem. Unfortunately, the existence of this variety of social welfare order, which we call anonymous Pareto, implies the existence of nonmeasurable sets of real numbers. For some, such as Litak, this entails that such social welfare orders are inadmissible for use in theoretical economics because they are non-constructive in nature. The authors seek to give nuance to this view, proving that anonymous Pareto and other social welfare orders can exist in the absence of nonprincipal ultrafilters over the set of natural numbers.
papers.title: There can be equitable social welfare orders but no fair voting system

papers.summary: Improving theorems of Bourgain and Badger--Genschaw, we prove that the Hausdorff dimension of harmonic measure on any domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, $\mathbb{R}^4$, and $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $n\geq3$ is at most $3-10^{-5}$, $4-10^{-7}$, and $n-(n-1)^{-(2n+6.12\sqrt{n})}$, respectively. The previous bounds in dimensions $3$ and $4$ were $3-10^{-15}$ and $4-10^{-26}$, while Bishop conjectures that the sharp bound is $n-(n-1)^{-1}$. The main difficulty in optimizing Bourgain's method is estimating non-additive $s$-dimensional Hausdorff-type contents when $s<n$ is close to $n$. Previous arguments used net contents associated to a fixed $m$-adic lattice, with $m$ large depending on $n$. We redevelop the dimension theory using pairwise disjoint cubes in general position and obtain a new estimate showing that one thin ring without large holes surrounding a cube makes it unlikely for Brownian motion to reach the cube before exiting the domain. A key feature of the construction is that the holes are round rather than rectangular. We also propose ten challenges on the dimension of harmonic measure that may provide accessible targets en route to Bishop's conjecture.
papers.title: One-Ring Bourgain Alternative And A 5-Decimal Bound On The Dimension Of Harmonic Measure

papers.summary: We consider the problem of reducing Zilber's pseudo-exponentiation conjecture to mere exponential-algebraic closedness, assuming Schanuel's conjecture but not Zilber-Pink. Generalising work of Mantova, we show that it would suffice to show that perfectly rotund varieties have non-dense intersection with finitely generated subgroups of the graph of exponentiation in which the exponentials live in a number field.
papers.title: SEAC from EAC modulo Schanuel: reduction to algebraic exponentials

papers.summary: We develop the general theory of Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories. We prove categorical versions of classical results such as Engel's theorem, Cartan's criterion, and that all derivations of a strongly semisimple Lie algebra are inner. For finite-dimensional graded Lie algebras, we construct a graded category $\mathcal{O}$, classify its graded-simple objects, and prove the generic graded irreducibility of Verma modules. Lastly, we develop the theory of root systems for contragredient Lie algebras.
papers.title: Lie algebras in symmetric tensor categories

papers.summary: The variety of semirings satisfying $x^2\approx x$ is hereditarily finitely based in the signature consisting of addition and multiplication, without designated constants. Multiplication may be noncommutative, and the semirings need not be finite. A subdirect decomposition reduces the proof to the subvarieties defined by $3x\approx x$ and $3x\approx2x$. In the latter case, we express each polynomial identity using a common doubled part and isolated word occurrences. Four fixed identities align the first- and last-occurrence words of these occurrences. Induction on their content extracts protected identities. The associated word identities define a band variety, to which the finite basis theorem for bands applies.
papers.title: The Finite Basis Problem for Multiplicatively Idempotent Semirings

papers.summary: A post-$3$-Lie algebra is a $3$-Lie algebra with an additional ternary multiplication, skew-symmetric in the first two arguments, related to the bracket by four compatibility identities. We give the algebraic and geometric classification of complex $2$- and $3$-dimensional post-$3$-Lie algebras and of complex $4$-dimensional nilpotent post-$3$-Lie algebras. The variety of $2$-dimensional algebras is irreducible of dimension $4$; the variety of $3$-dimensional algebras has dimension $12$ and $12$ irreducible components, and exactly one rigid algebra; the variety of $4$-dimensional nilpotent algebras has dimension $14$, two irreducible components and no rigid algebras.
papers.title: The algebraic and geometric classification of post-$3$-Lie algebras

papers.summary: We prove that the conjugacy problem in finitely presented metabelian groups with a fixed number of generators is solvable in bounded-error quantum polynomial time, uniformly in the defining relations of the group. Both the group presentation and the words representing the elements are part of the input. The main ingredient is a quantum polynomial-time algorithm for computing all multiplicative relations among a fixed number of units in a commutative affine $\mathbb Z$-algebra presented with a fixed number of variables. The algorithm reduces the problem to computations in finite-dimensional algebras over $\mathbb Q$ and finite rings by identifying the lattice of exponent vectors whose corresponding products are algebraic over the coefficient field. An effective arithmetic splitting combines the rational and finite-ring computations. The proof uses effective bounds for polynomial equations, algorithms for finite-dimensional commutative algebras, quantum integer factorization, and finite abelian hidden-subgroup algorithms.
papers.title: Quantum polynomial-time conjugacy in metabelian groups

papers.summary: We continue the study of the octonionic spectrum of the octonionic structure operator $h$ on $W=\mathbb O\otimes_{\mathbb R}V$, where $V$ is the seven-dimensional representation of $G_2$. The real spectrum and the octonionic one-step spectrum, given by the equation $h(w)=wλ$ for real or octonion $λ$, have been determined in earlier work. In this paper, we study the two-step equation $h(w)=(wλ_1)λ_2$. Due to non-associativity, this does not in general reduce to the one-step problem. An adapted quaternionic frame represents successive right multiplication by an operator with four real coefficients. The $SU(2)$ subgroup fixing the frame splits $W$ into invariant sectors of dimensions $16$, $12$ and $28$. We factor the determinant of the resulting 4-parameter operator pencil and characterize the pairs for which a nonzero solution exists. The singular locus of this pencil in $\mathbb R^4$ is the union of an explicit algebraic set and a round $3$-sphere. The $12$-dimensional sector carries the one-step problem at the reversed product $λ_2λ_1$. The $28$-dimensional sector contributes no additional real singular points; the fixed sector produces solutions even when neither product lies in the one-step right spectrum.
papers.title: The two-step spectral locus of the octonionic structure operator
